title: Questions and answers
scope: Question words क्या, कौन, कैसा, कितना, क्यों; adjective agreement with mixed genders and with आप and तुम; भी and न; honorific and numerical plurals; greetings and polite words

lessons.title: क्या, कौन, कैसा, कितना, क्यों
lessons.desc: Pick the right question word and its form

items.q: Fill the gap: “What is this?”
items.why: The question is about a thing, so it takes क्या.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who is that girl?”
wrong: क्या asks “what?” about a thing (at the very start of a sentence it instead turns the sentence into a yes/no question).
कितनी is the -ī form of कितना, for feminine words.
items.why: The question is about a person, so it takes कौन.

items.q: Fill the gap: “How are you? (to a man)”
wrong: कैसा (“what kind of, how”) in its -ā form goes only with a masculine singular word.
items.why: आप is grammatically plural, so कैसा takes its -e form, कैसे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What is the weather like?”
wrong: कैसी is the -ī form of कैसा, for feminine words.
कैसे is the -e form of कैसा, for masculine plurals and for आप and तुम.
items.why: मौसम is masculine singular, so कैसा keeps its -ā form.

items.q: Fill the gap: “How many female students are here?”
wrong: कितने (“how many”) is the -e form of कितना, for masculine plurals.
कितना (“how much”) in its -ā form goes with a masculine singular word.
items.why: छात्राएँ is feminine, so it takes कितनी.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Why is Sangeeta upset?”
wrong: कैसी is the -ī form of कैसा, for feminine words.
items.why: Asking for a reason needs क्यों.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What is that thick book?”
wrong: कितनी is the -ī form of कितना, for feminine words.
items.why: The question is about a thing, so it takes क्या.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What kind of shoes are these?”
wrong: कैसी is the -ī form of कैसा, for feminine words.
कैसा (“what kind of, how”) in its -ā form goes only with a masculine singular word.
items.why: जूते is masculine plural, so it takes कैसे.

items.q: Fill the gap: “What kind of letter is that?”
wrong: कैसा (“what kind of, how”) in its -ā form goes only with a masculine singular word.
कैसे is the -e form of कैसा, for masculine plurals and for आप and तुम.
items.why: चिट्ठी is feminine, so it takes कैसी.

items.q: Fill the gap: “How expensive is the dictionary?”
wrong: कितनी is the -ī form of कितना, for feminine words.
कितने (“how many”) is the -e form of कितना, for masculine plurals.
items.why: शब्दकोश is masculine singular, so it takes कितना, just like महँगा.

items.q: Fill the gap: “How many students are there today?”
wrong: कितना (“how much”) in its -ā form goes with a masculine singular word.
कितनी is the -ī form of कितना, for feminine words.
items.why: A count of students (a group, or male students) takes the masculine plural कितने.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Who are you?”
wrong: क्या asks “what?” about a thing (at the very start of a sentence it instead turns the sentence into a yes/no question).
items.why: The question is about a person, so it takes कौन.

lessons.title: Agreement
lessons.desc: Mixed genders, आप and तुम, invariable adjectives

items.q: Fill the gap: “Pratap and Sangeeta are tall.”
wrong: लंबी is feminine. Sangeeta alone would take it, but a mixed group of people takes the masculine plural.
लंबा is masculine singular, but the subject is two people.
items.why: A group of people of mixed gender takes the masculine plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “These shoes and sandals are new.”
items.say: ये जूते और चप्पलें नई हैं ।
items.en: These[0] shoes[1] and[2] sandals[3] are[5] new[4].
wrong: नए would agree with जूते, but with things of mixed gender the adjective agrees with the nearest noun, चप्पलें.
नया is masculine singular, but the subject is plural.
items.why: With things of mixed gender, the adjective agrees with the nearest noun. चप्पलें is feminine.

items.q: Fill the gap: “These books and newspapers are old.”
items.say: ये किताबें और अख़बार पुराने हैं ।
items.en: These[0] books[1] and[2] newspapers[3] are[5] old[4].
wrong: पुरानी would agree with किताबें, but the nearest noun is अख़बार, which is masculine.
पुराना is masculine singular, but there are several newspapers.
items.why: With things of mixed gender, the adjective agrees with the nearest noun. अख़बार here is masculine plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You are very tall. (to a man)”
items.en: You[0] are[3] very[1] tall[2]. (to a man)
wrong: आप is grammatically plural, so even for one man the adjective takes the plural -e form.
लंबी would suit a woman, but this is said to a man.
items.why: आप is grammatically plural, so the adjective is plural too.

items.q: Fill the gap: “How are you? (to a woman)”
wrong: कैसे is right for a man or a group. A woman is addressed with the feminine कैसी.
कैसा is masculine singular, and आप is grammatically plural in any case.
items.why: Feminine forms stay -ī in the plural, so a woman is asked आप कैसी हैं ?

items.q: Fill the gap: “You are a good daughter.”
wrong: अच्छे is the -e form, which goes with masculine plural nouns and with आप, तुम and respected people.
अच्छा is the -ā form, which goes only with a masculine singular noun.
items.why: बेटी is feminine, so the adjective takes -ī.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You are a good son.”
wrong: With तुम, a masculine noun in -ā shows its -e plural even for one person.
items.why: तुम is grammatically plural, so बेटा becomes बेटे, as in तुम लड़के.

items.q: Fill the gap: “You are good daughters.”
wrong: बेटी is one daughter. Feminine nouns show their plural only when there really are several.
items.why: There are several daughters, so the numerical plural बेटियाँ is needed.

items.q: Fill the gap: “That book is very expensive.”
wrong: महँगा is the -ā form, which goes only with a masculine singular noun.
महँगे is the -e form, which goes with masculine plural nouns and with आप, तुम and respected people.
items.why: किताब is feminine.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This dictionary is cheap.”
wrong: सस्ती is the -ī form, which goes with feminine nouns, singular or plural.
सस्ते is the -e form, which goes with masculine plural nouns and with आप, तुम and respected people.
items.why: शब्दकोश is masculine singular.

items.q: Fill the gap: “The air is dirty.”
wrong: गंदा is the -ā form, which goes only with a masculine singular noun.
गंदे is the -e form, which goes with masculine plural nouns and with आप, तुम and respected people.
items.why: हवा ends in -ā but is feminine, so the adjective takes -ī.

items.q: Fill the gap: “That girl is happy.”
wrong: ख़ुश never changes. ख़ुशी is a different word, a noun meaning “happiness”.
ख़ुश never changes, so this is not a real form.
items.why: Adjectives that do not end in -ā, like ख़ुश, never change.

items.q: Fill the gap: “This is a new newspaper.”
wrong: नई is the -ī form, which goes with feminine nouns, singular or plural.
नए is the -e form, which goes with masculine plural nouns and with आप, तुम and respected people.
items.why: अख़बार is masculine singular.

items.q: Fill the gap: “two dirty shoes”
wrong: गंदा is the -ā form, which goes only with a masculine singular noun.
गंदी is the -ī form, which goes with feminine nouns, singular or plural.
items.why: जूते is masculine plural.

items.q: Fill the gap: “Mrs Sharma is strict.”
wrong: सख़्त never changes, so this is not a real form.
सख़्त never changes, so this is not a real form.
items.why: Adjectives that do not end in -ā, like सख़्त, never change.

lessons.title: More plurals
lessons.desc: New nouns, honorific and real plurals

items.q: Pick the plural of “female student” (feminine)
wrong: -ẽ is added to the whole word, so छात्रा keeps its -ā.
-iyā̃ belongs to feminine nouns ending in -ī.
This is the singular. Feminine nouns change in the plural.
items.why: Feminine nouns that do not end in -ī add -ẽ, even when they end in -ā.

items.q: Pick the plural of “daughter” (feminine)
wrong: Feminine nouns in -ī do not just add -ẽ.
बेटे is the plural of बेटा, “son”.
items.why: Feminine nouns ending in -ī change it to -iyā̃.

items.q: Pick the plural of “letter” (feminine)
wrong: Feminine nouns in -ī do not just add -ẽ.
The -e plural is for masculine nouns in -ā.
items.why: Feminine nouns ending in -ī change it to -iyā̃.

items.q: Pick the plural of “sandal” (feminine)
wrong: -iyā̃ belongs to feminine nouns ending in -ī.
The -e plural is for masculine nouns in -ā.
items.why: Feminine nouns that do not end in -ī add -ẽ.

items.q: Pick the plural of “sister” (feminine)
wrong: -iyā̃ belongs to feminine nouns ending in -ī.
The -e plural is for masculine nouns in -ā.
items.why: Feminine nouns that do not end in -ī add -ẽ.

items.q: Pick the plural of “shoe” (masculine)
wrong: This is the singular. Masculine nouns in -ā change.
items.why: Masculine nouns ending in -ā change it to -e.

items.q: Pick the plural of “son” (masculine)
items.why: Masculine nouns ending in -ā change it to -e.

items.q: Pick the plural of “brother” (masculine)
wrong: Only masculine nouns ending in -ā take -e.
items.why: Masculine nouns that do not end in -ā stay the same in the plural.

items.q: Pick the plural of “newspaper” (masculine)
wrong: -ẽ is a feminine plural ending, and अख़बार is masculine.
Only masculine nouns ending in -ā take -e.
items.why: Masculine nouns that do not end in -ā stay the same in the plural.

items.q: Pick the plural of “question” (masculine)
wrong: -ẽ is a feminine plural ending, and सवाल is masculine.
Only masculine nouns ending in -ā take -e.
items.why: Masculine nouns that do not end in -ā stay the same in the plural.

items.q: तुम अच्छे बेटे हो । can mean…
items.a: “You are a good son” or “You are good sons”
wrong: With तुम, बेटा takes its -e form even for one son, so the sentence fits one son too.
बेटे is also the ordinary plural, so the sentence fits several sons too.
items.why: With तुम, masculine nouns in -ā show -e for one person as well as for several. लोग can be added to make a plural clear.

items.q: तुम अच्छी बेटी हो । can mean…
wrong: For several daughters the noun itself becomes plural: बेटियाँ.
Feminine nouns show the plural only when there really are several, so बेटी means one.
items.why: Feminine nouns change only for a real (numerical) plural.

wrong: क्या asks “what?”. For a person, use कौन.
हैं goes with plural or respected subjects. One man spoken of plainly takes है.

items.en: How[1] are[2] you[0]? (formal, to a man)
wrong: आप is grammatically plural, so it needs कैसे, not the singular कैसा.
हो goes only with तुम. आप takes हैं.
सस्ती is feminine, but अख़बार is masculine.
हैं is plural. One newspaper takes है.
गंदे is masculine plural, but चप्पलें is feminine.
है is singular. Several sandals take हैं.
हैं is plural. One student spoken of plainly takes है.
क्यों means “why”, which is not in the sentence.
items.order: भी follows the word it qualifies. “The student too” is विद्यार्थी भी, and the verb comes last.

wrong: कौन means “who”, but the question asks “why”.
हैं is plural. Kamala spoken of plainly takes है.
कितने is masculine plural, but लड़कियाँ is feminine.
है is singular. Several girls take हैं.
हैं is plural. मौसम is singular.
कैसा means “what like?”, but this sentence is a statement.
A mixed group of people takes the masculine plural, लंबे.
है is singular. Two people take हैं.

items.en: Is[3] the book[1] new[2] or[4] old[5]?
wrong: नया is masculine, but किताब is feminine.
हैं is plural. One book takes है.
है goes with one person or thing. हम takes हैं.

items.en: That[0] is[4] not[3] a bad[1] thing[2].
wrong: बुरा is masculine, but बात is feminine.
बुरे is masculine plural, but बात is feminine singular.

lessons.title: What does it mean?
lessons.desc: Read a sentence, pick the translation

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: शब्दकोश सस्ता है, लेकिन किताब महँगी है ।
items.a: The dictionary is cheap, but the book is expensive.
wrong: The dictionary is expensive, but the book is cheap.
सस्ता (“cheap”) goes with शब्दकोश and महँगी (“expensive”) with किताब.
The dictionary and the book are both cheap.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: A plain yes/no question would start with क्या. कितने asks for a number.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.a: Everything is fine at the moment.
wrong: “Today” is आज. अभी means “at the moment, right now”.
There is no क्या or question mark, so this is a statement.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: भाई बीमार है और बहिन भी बीमार है ।
items.a: The brother is ill and the sister is ill too.
wrong: The brother is ill, but the sister is well.
और means “and”, and भी बीमार means “ill too”.
This is a statement, and भी follows बहिन, not भाई.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: This answer is not right at all.
बिलकुल नहीं would mean “not at all”. Here बिलकुल means “completely”.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.a: Most of the female students are Japanese.
wrong: Most of the boys are Japanese.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
items.hi: प्रदूषण बहुत ख़राब है, पर हवा आज साफ़ है ।
items.a: Pollution is very bad, but the air is clean today.
wrong: Pollution is very bad, and the air is dirty today.
This is a statement, not a question.

items.q: What does this sentence mean?
wrong: That would be आप कैसे हैं ? कौन asks “who”.
That would be यह क्या है ? आप means “you”.

items.q: Which sentence means “Rishi is ill too” (as well as someone else)?
wrong: भी qualifies the word just before it. Here that is बीमार, so this means Rishi is ill as well as being something else.
भी never comes first. It follows the word it qualifies.
items.why: भी (“also, too”) qualifies the word immediately before it.

items.q: Which sentence means “The book is cheap too” (as well as good)?
wrong: Here भी follows किताब, so it means the book too is cheap, as well as other things.
भी never comes first. It follows the word it qualifies.
items.why: भी (“also, too”) qualifies the word immediately before it.

items.q: What does न add at the end of this sentence?
items.a: It asks the listener to agree: “…aren't you?”
wrong: It makes the sentence negative: “You aren't Indian.”
A negative needs नहीं before the verb. न after the sentence asks for agreement.
It turns it into a plain yes/no question, like क्या
A plain yes/no question starts with क्या. न at the end expects the answer “yes”.
items.why: After a statement, न works like “isn't it?” or the French “n'est-ce pas?”.

items.q: What does this greeting mean?
wrong: That would be यह क्या है ? हाल means “condition”.
That would be मौसम कैसा है ?
items.why: क्या हाल है ? is literally “what is the condition?”, a casual “how are things?”.

items.q: Which word is the formal “please”?
wrong: मेहरबानी means “kindness”; मेहरबानी है is a way of saying “thank you”.

items.q: Which greeting is the formal one?
wrong: हलो is a casual loanword greeting.
items.why: नमस्ते and नमस्कार are the formal greetings, usually said with the hands folded.

items.q: What does लोग add in this sentence?
items.a: It makes clear that several people are meant
wrong: आप or जी show respect. लोग marks a real plural of several people.
It turns the sentence into a question
Nothing here is a question; क्या or a question word would be needed.
items.why: Since वे can be a respectful way to refer to one person, adding लोग makes the number clear.

items.q: आप कैसे हैं ? can be said to…
items.a: one man, or a group of people
wrong: आप is grammatically plural, so कैसे fits one man as well.
A woman is asked आप कैसी हैं ?
items.why: आप is grammatically plural, so its adjective is plural whether one or many are meant.

items.q: What does मालूम नहीं mean?
wrong: That would need धन्यवाद or शुक्रिया.
items.why: मालूम नहीं is literally “not known”.

items.q: How does जी change शर्मा जी compared with plain शर्मा?
wrong: Mrs is श्रीमती, placed before the name.
जी adds respect; it says nothing about family.
items.why: जी after a name is polite and cordial, about as formal as आप.
